title: Advanced Probability
relevance: Quant and top-tier product interviews use these problems to test whether candidates can simplify with Bayes, symmetry, complements, and recursive states rather than grind brute-force enumeration.

phases.goal: Establish the core probability identities candidates must recite and apply before any puzzle.

must_hit.point: Conditional probability and Bayes' theorem: P(A|B)=P(A∩B)/P(B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes Bayes with prior, likelihood, and marginal; does not treat accuracy as the posterior.

must_hit.point: Law of total probability: P(A)=∑ P(A|B_i)P(B_i) for any partition B_i of the sample space.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Expands P(positive test) or P(HHH) by conditioning on disease/coin type or similar partition.

must_hit.point: Independence means P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B); the complement rule is P(A)=1-P(A^c), and 'at least one' problems should go through 1-P(none).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the product rule for independence and explicitly routes 'at least one' through the complement.

probes: State Bayes' theorem and the law of total probability, and explain when you would use the complement instead of enumerating 'at least one' outcomes.

hints.1: Start from the definitions in the core rules block—conditional probability, total probability, independence, complement.
hints.2: Write P(A|B) two ways (intersection form and Bayes form), then expand P(B) by partitioning.
hints.3: Say: P(A|B)=P(B|A)P(A)/P(B); P(A)=∑P(A|B_i)P(B_i); independent iff P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B); for 'at least one' use 1-P(none).

phases.goal: Show how Bayes updates, sample-space conditioning, and symmetry/recursion produce exact answers on classic puzzles.

must_hit.point: Disease base-rate paradox: prior 1 in 10000, 99% accurate test both ways; P(disease|positive)≈0.0098≈1%, not 99%.
Two-children 'at least one boy' yields 1/3; adding 'boy born on a Tuesday' changes the conditional space to 13/27.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Reduces {BB,BG,GB,GG} to three equally likely outcomes for 1/3; for Tuesday boy counts 196 pairs, |A|=27, BB∩A=13.

must_hit.point: Monty Hall: switching wins with probability 2/3 because the initial pick is a goat with probability 2/3 and the host then forces the car onto the remaining door.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says initial car prob 1/3, goat 2/3; switch wins exactly when the initial pick was a goat.

must_hit.point: Symmetry/complement shortcuts: first Ace before first King is 4/8=1/2; 3 Heads before 2 Tails equals at least 3 Heads in 4 flips = 5/16; Alice first-to-six wins with 36/91.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Ignores the other 44 cards and uses equal chance among 8 targets; or maps race to 4-flip count; or sets P(A)+(5/6)P(A)+(25/36)P(A)=1.

must_hit.point: State recursion: fair gambler from $5 to hit $10 before $0 is k/N=5/10=1/2; unfair p=2/3 from $1 to $3 gives P_1=4/7; HH vs TH race gives Bob 3/4.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses absorbing-boundary k/N for fair ruin, solves the P_1/P_2 system for unfair, and cases on first flip for the pattern race.

probes: A disease affects 1 in 10000 people; a test is 99% accurate both ways. If you test positive, what is P(you have the disease), and why is the intuitive 99% wrong?

hints.1: Name the events D and T+, write Bayes, and expand P(T+) with the law of total probability.
hints.2: Plug in P(D)=0.0001, P(T+|D)=0.99, P(T+|D^c)=0.01 and compare true positives to false positives.
hints.3: Arrive at ≈0.0098≈1%: false positives from the huge healthy population overwhelm the rare true positives.

phases.goal: Choose the right simplification—symmetry, complement, spinning vs conditioning, or probability vs expectation—instead of brute force.

must_hit.point: Prefer symmetry or a recursive state over grinding an infinite series when events are symmetric; say the shortcut out loud.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions ignoring irrelevant cards/games or defining a first-step state instead of summing an infinite geometric series blindly.

must_hit.point: Russian Roulette with two adjacent bullets: after a click, surviving without spinning is 3/4 vs 2/3 if you respin—so do not spin.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Conditions on which of the four empties was just fired; 3 of 4 next chambers are empty, beating the unconditional 2/3 survival from a fresh spin.

must_hit.point: Do not confuse expected flips until a pattern with the probability that one pattern appears before another.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States that EV answers a time/count question while a race answers a likelihood ≤1 (e.g. Bob wins HH-vs-TH with 3/4).

probes: In the adjacent-bullet Russian Roulette setup, after the first player gets a click, should you spin again or pull immediately—and what are the two survival probabilities?

hints.1: Compare a fresh uniform chamber draw to conditioning on the fact the previous chamber was empty.
hints.2: With cylinder BBEEEE, label the four empties and see what follows each; spinning resets to 2 bullets in 6.
hints.3: Survival without spinning is 3/4; with spinning is 2/3; therefore do not spin.

phases.goal: Transfer the same tools to geometric sample spaces, combinatorial draws, and OA-style word problems.

must_hit.point: Geometric probability: broken stick forms a triangle with probability 1/4; friends waiting 15 minutes in a 60-minute window meet with probability 7/16; random B,C in [-1,1] give real roots with probability 13/24.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Argues via area in the unit square / 60×60 square / discriminant region, citing those three answers.

must_hit.point: Combinatorial draws: hypergeometric 2 red and 2 blue from 5 red+7 blue when drawing 4 is 14/33; derangement of 4 names has probability 3/8.
OA Bayes variant: 2% bots, filter catches 95% of bots and falsely flags 3% of humans; P(human|flagged)≈61%.
Packet routing trick: put 1 red alone in one queue and 49 red+50 blue in the other to get red with probability 74/99; birthday paradox with 23 people and 365 days is about 50% via the complement.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Gives the 1-vs-rest split and 1/2+(1/2)(49/99)=74/99; for birthdays uses 1−P(all different)≈1−0.493≈0.507.

probes: An AI filter flags 95% of the 2% bot traffic but also 3% of humans. If a session is flagged, roughly what is P(it is actually human), and which multiple-choice ballpark does that land in?

hints.1: Treat this as Bayes with prior P(bot)=0.02 and false-positive rate 0.03 on humans.
hints.2: Compute P(flagged) from bots and humans separately, then take the human contribution over the total.

tradeoffs.topic: Symmetry/recursion shortcut vs brute-force infinite series
tradeoffs.strong_answer: When outcomes are symmetric or Markovian, ignore irrelevant padding (other cards/games) or define a first-step state; grinding the full series is unnecessary once the shortcut is visible, and interviewers want that simplification spoken aloud.

tradeoffs.topic: Respin vs pull after a click (Russian Roulette)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Spinning restores unconditional survival 2/3 (2 bullets in 6 chambers). Not spinning conditions on the prior empty chamber among four empties, yielding survival 3/4. Because 3/4>2/3, do not spin.

tradeoffs.topic: Pattern-appearance probability vs expected waiting time
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Expected flips until HH is a waiting-time number; P(HH before TH) is a race probability (Bob wins with 3/4). Solving the EV equation does not answer the before/after likelihood question.

gotchas.trap: Base-rate neglect: guessing ~99% that a positive disease test means you have the disease.
gotchas.correction: With prior 1 in 10000, false positives (~1% of ~9999 healthy people) dominate true positives (99% of ~1 sick person), so P(D|T+)≈1%.

gotchas.trap: Confusing 'expected flips until HH' with 'probability HH appears before TH'.
gotchas.correction: Expectation answers how long you wait; the race answers who wins. For fair flips, Bob's TH beats Alice's HH with probability 3/4.

gotchas.trap: Treating 'at least one shared birthday' by counting people instead of using the complement.
gotchas.correction: Compute 1−P(all 23 birthdays distinct) over 365 days (≈0.507≈50%), noting 23 people make 253 pairs so collisions arrive sooner than intuition suggests.
